oneLine: Solid, accurate glosses, translations and chat with sensible corrections; let down by a wrong clitic analysis of 'se me olvidó', every question card missing the opening '¿', and a false 'cuáles + noun' rule.

mistakes.item: olvidó (Se me olvidó la llave en casa.)
mistakes.what: Clitics list only 'me' with role "accidental se"; 'me' is the indirect object (the person affected) and the accidental 'se' itself is missing from the analysis.

mistakes.item: olvidó (Se me olvidó la llave en casa.)
mistakes.what: Phrase given as "olvidarse de" = "to forget about something", which is not the construction in this sentence (se me olvidó + subject 'la llave'); no note that the key is the grammatical subject.
grammarNote "In Latin America, 'dáselo' is standard in the 'tú' imperative" is filler that implies a regional difference where there is none; otherMeanings "to happen" is doubtful for dar.

mistakes.item: echar (Voy a echar de menos a mi familia.)
mistakes.what: No note that in Latin America 'extrañar' is the everyday verb for 'to miss' and 'echar de menos' sounds Spain-leaning.

mistakes.item: llevo (Llevo dos años viviendo en Monterrey.)
mistakes.what: The 'llevar + time + gerund' construction is not flagged as a phrase or explained in a grammar note; lemmaMeaning just "to carry".

mistakes.item: quedé (Me quedé en casa porque llovía.)
mistakes.what: Flags "quedarse en casa" as an idiom/phrase although it is plain compositional usage.
Only 9 cards, three of them present tense; about 10 expected.

mistakes.item: Cuando éramos niños, tú siempre ___ feliz.
mistakes.what: English "you were always happy" (a lasting trait) does not clearly rule out 'eras feliz' (ser), so the card is ambiguous.
'ya ... antes' is redundant and 'ya' has nothing in the English to match it.

mistakes.item: all question-word cards (e.g. "___ paciencia tiene usted con él?")
mistakes.what: Every question in deck 1 is missing the opening '¿' (answers like "Cuánta" don't carry it either), which teaches wrong punctuation.

Note "Use cuáles before plural nouns when asking which" is false as a rule (the standard is 'qué + noun': ¿Qué restaurantes...?), and it contradicts the model's own 'Qué materia' note "Before a noun, what is translated as qué".
Again 'cuáles + noun' where 'qué calles' is the standard form. Colloquial at best. There is no proper 'cuál es...' card.
The Spanish uses usted ('le pone') but the English has no '(formal)' tag, unlike the other usted cards.

mistakes.item: Yo ___ mis llaves en la mesa de la cocina. (he dejado)
mistakes.what: Mexican usage would normally use the preterite 'dejé' here; the present perfect sounds Spain-leaning.
Deck 2 has 9 cards (19 in all versus about 20 expected).

mistakes.item: Ayer comí en un restaurante y el comida es muy bueno.
mistakes.what: Keeps present 'es' in a past narrative ('estuvo/era' would fit 'Ayer'); acceptable as a minimal correction but missed.

strengths: Correct lemmas on all the trap words: fui=ir, fue=ser, vino=noun, como=comer.
dáselo clitics (se = IO replacing le, lo = DO) and formation are correct.
'Me da pena' correctly glossed as embarrassment with a Latin American note.
Sentence translations are accurate, every target idiom is caught, and nothing is invented for 'El perro come pan'.
Drill Spanish is natural, with correct estar forms, and the English forces the tense in most cards.
Chat replies are short, natural and Mexican (pozole rojo o blanco); corrections fix exactly the errors and leave sentences 3 and 4 alone.
